title: Lexicographically Smallest String After Operations With Constraint
summary: Given a string s and an integer k, find the lexicographically smallest string t that can be formed by changing any letter of s to any other lowercase English letter, ensuring the distance between s and t is less than or equal to k.
statement: Given a string s and an integer k, find the lexicographically smallest string t that can be formed by changing any letter of s to any other lowercase English letter, ensuring the distance between s and t is less than or equal to k.
constraints: s contains lowercase letters and k is nonnegative.
Changing one character costs its shortest circular alphabet distance, where a and z are adjacent.
Spend total cost at most k and return the lexicographically smallest obtainable string.
hints: Lexicographic order makes the earliest improvable position more important than every later character combined.
Scan left to right and choose the smallest letter reachable within the remaining circular-distance budget.
For candidate letters a through the current character, take the first with min(backward,wrap)≤k, subtract its cost, and continue.
The first differing position dominates lexicographic comparison, so the locally smallest affordable choice cannot be improved by saving budget for later.
editorial: The first differing position dominates lexicographic comparison, so the locally smallest affordable choice cannot be improved by saving budget for later.

tests.explanation: Change z to a for one and both b characters to a for one each, leaving the final z and producing aaaz.
Changing the first x to a costs three, so the best use is changing it backward by two to v, producing vax.
